The second overtone is the **third harmonic**, with **4 nodes** and **3 antinodes**.
**Step 1 — translate the name.**
fundamental = **first** harmonic ✓
first overtone = **second** harmonic ✓
second overtone = **third** harmonic ✓
**Step 2 — picture the third harmonic.** The string carries **three** half-waves:
L = **3λ/2** ✓
**Step 3 — count the nodes.** Both fixed ends are nodes, and there are two more inside:
**4 nodes** ✓
**Step 4 — count the antinodes.** One at the centre of each half-wave loop:
**3 antinodes** ✓
**The pattern in general.** For the **n**th harmonic:
loops = **n** ✓
antinodes = **n** ✓
nodes = **n + 1** ✓
There is always exactly **one more node than antinode**, because the loops are separated
by nodes and bounded by them at each end.
**The sketch.**
N - A - N - A - N - A - N ✓
nodes and antinodes alternating, beginning and ending with a node at the clamped ends.
**Why the ends must be nodes.** They are **fixed**, so the displacement there is
permanently zero ✓ This boundary condition is what quantises the allowed wavelengths and
produces a discrete harmonic series rather than a continuum.
**The frequency.**
f₃ = 3v/2L = **3f₁** ✓ three times the fundamental - an octave and a fifth above it.
**The spacings.** Adjacent nodes are **λ/2 = L/3** apart; a node and the next antinode
**λ/4 = L/6** ✓
**Why "overtone" and "harmonic" differ by one.** "Harmonic" counts the fundamental as
the first; "overtone" counts it as none, the overtones being what lie **above** it ✓
The off-by-one is the single commonest error in this topic, and the whole difficulty of
this question.
**Why a string gives all harmonics.** Both ends are nodes, so L = nλ/2 for every
integer n ✓ A pipe closed at one end, by contrast, gives only the odd ones.
**How a player selects a harmonic.** Touching a violin string lightly at a node - a
third of the way along, here - suppresses the fundamental and leaves the third
harmonic ✓ This is how harmonics are played, and it confirms the node positions
directly.
**Reading the distractors.** **3 and 2** ✗ describes the **second** harmonic - the
answer if "second overtone" is misread as "second harmonic". **3 and 4** ✗ reverses the
counts, and **2 and 3** ✗ gives fewer nodes than antinodes, which is impossible on a
string fixed at both ends ✓
∴ 4 and 3.

Falling from rest, v = √(2gH), so λ = h/mv goes as **H⁻¹ᐟ²**.
**Step 1 — find the speed after falling H.**
v = **√(2gH)** ✓
**Step 2 — write the momentum.**
p = mv = **m√(2gH)** ✓
**Step 3 — write the de Broglie wavelength.**
λ = h/p = **h/(m√(2gH))** ✓
**Step 4 — read off the dependence.**
λ ∝ **1/√H = H⁻¹ᐟ²** ✓
**Why the wavelength shrinks as it falls.** The particle **speeds up**, so its momentum
grows and λ = h/p falls ✓ Quadrupling the drop halves the wavelength.
**The relation in full.**
λ = **h/(m√(2gH))** ✓
Everything but H is constant for a given particle, so the proportionality is exact.
**A worked instance.** An electron dropped 1 m:
v = √(2 x 9·8 x 1) = **4·43 m s⁻¹** ✓
λ = 6·63 x 10⁻³⁴/(9·11 x 10⁻³¹ x 4·43) = **1·64 x 10⁻⁴ m** ✓ a sixth of a millimetre -
remarkably large, because the electron is so slow and so light.
**The same for a 1 g bead.**
λ = 6·63 x 10⁻³⁴/(10⁻³ x 4·43) = **1·5 x 10⁻³¹ m** ✓ unimaginably smaller than a nucleus,
which is why no wave behaviour is ever seen in falling objects.
**Why mass matters so much.** λ ∝ **1/m** ✓ and macroscopic masses exceed atomic ones by
twenty-odd orders of magnitude, which is the whole reason the quantum world is hidden
from everyday experience.
**Why the relation is a power law at all.** Both the kinetic-energy relation and the de
Broglie relation are power laws ✓
K = mgH, p = √(2mK), λ = h/p
so λ ∝ K⁻¹ᐟ² ∝ H⁻¹ᐟ².
**The useful general form.**
λ = **h/√(2mK)** ✓ which also gives λ = 12·27/√V Å for an electron accelerated through
V volts - the formula behind the Davisson-Germer experiment.
**Why air resistance is ignored.** The question says "dropped", implying free fall ✓
With drag the speed would approach a terminal value and λ would tend to a **constant**,
an H⁰ dependence - which is where the second option comes from.
**Reading the distractors.** **H⁰** ✗ would mean the wavelength never changes, though
the particle plainly accelerates. **H** ✗ and **H¹ᐟ²** ✗ make λ **grow** as it speeds up,
inverting λ = h/p ✓
∴ H⁻¹/².

A hydrogen-like ion scales as **Z²**; the first excitation energy fixes Z, and then the
ionisation energy follows.
**Step 1 — write the levels.**
E_n = **−13·6Z²/n² eV** ✓
**Step 2 — write the first excitation energy.** From n = 1 to n = 2:
ΔE = 13·6Z²(1 − 1/4) = **10·2Z² eV** ✓
**Step 3 — set it equal to 40·8 eV.**
10·2Z² = 40·8
Z² = 4, so **Z = 2** ✓ a singly ionised **helium** ion, He⁺.
**Step 4 — find the ionisation energy from the ground state.**
E_ion = **13·6Z²** = 13·6 x 4
= **54·4 eV** ✓
**The quick route.** Ionisation energy and first excitation energy always stand in the
ratio
13·6Z² : 10·2Z² = **4 : 3** ✓
so E_ion = (4/3) x 40·8 = **54·4 eV** ✓ without ever finding Z.
**Why the Z² scaling.** The nucleus attracts the electron **Z** times more strongly, and
the orbit shrinks by a factor **Z** ✓ Both effects multiply the energy, giving Z². The
radius is correspondingly a₀/Z = 0·265 Å for He⁺.
**What "hydrogen-like" means.** **One** electron only ✓ He⁺, Li²⁺, Be³⁺ and so on. With
two or more electrons, their mutual repulsion spoils the simple formula and the Bohr
model fails.
**The level diagram for He⁺.**
n = 1: **−54·4 eV** ✓
n = 2: **−13·6 eV** ✓
n = 3: **−6·04 eV** ✓
and 54·4 − 13·6 = **40·8 eV**, the stated excitation energy ✓ confirming Z = 2.
**The coincidence worth noticing.** He⁺'s n = 2 level sits at **−13·6 eV**, exactly
hydrogen's ground state ✓ because −13·6Z²/n² = −13·6(4)/4. Such coincidences recur
whenever n/Z is the same.
**Why the ionisation energy is the ground-state binding energy.** Removing the electron
means taking it to **n = ∞**, where E = 0 ✓ so the energy required is simply |E₁|.
**The wavelength of that first excitation.**
λ = 1240/40·8 = **30·4 nm** ✓ far ultraviolet, as expected for an ion four times more
tightly bound than hydrogen.
**Reading the distractors.** **40·8 eV** ✗ is the excitation energy itself, not the
ionisation energy. **13·6 eV** ✗ is hydrogen's value, ignoring Z. **27·2 eV** ✗ is
13·6 x 2, using Z rather than Z² ✓
∴ 54.4 eV.

The Kaiga station generates electricity for the grid, so it is a **power reactor**.
**Step 1 — recall the plant.** Kaiga is in **Uttara Kannada** district, Karnataka, on the
Kali river ✓ operated by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India.
**Step 2 — recall its purpose.** It feeds the **southern grid** ✓ Its units are
**pressurised heavy-water reactors** (PHWRs) of 220 MW each, four of them, giving
**880 MW** in all.
**Step 3 — classify.** A reactor built to generate electricity is a **power reactor** ✓
**Why it is not a research reactor.** Research reactors - **Apsara**, **Cirus**,
**Dhruva** at Trombay - produce **neutrons** for experiments, isotope production and
materials testing ✓ They are small, run at low power, and generate no electricity.
**Why it is not a breeder.** A **breeder** produces more fissile material than it
consumes ✓ India's is the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at **Kalpakkam**, part of the
three-stage programme that aims to exploit the country's large **thorium** reserves.
**Why it is not a fusion reactor.** No fusion reactor anywhere yet generates net power ✓
**ITER**, under construction in France with Indian participation, is the first intended
to.
**How a PHWR works.** **Natural uranium** fuel with **heavy water** as both moderator and
coolant ✓ Heavy water absorbs far fewer neutrons than ordinary water, so natural uranium
suffices and no enrichment plant is needed - the reason India chose this design.
**Why a moderator is needed.** Fission neutrons emerge **fast**, at about 2 MeV, but
U-235 fissions most readily with **slow** (thermal) neutrons ✓ The moderator slows them
by repeated elastic collisions with light nuclei.
**The chain reaction.**
²³⁵U + n → fission fragments + **2 or 3 neutrons** + **200 MeV** ✓
Control rods of cadmium or boron absorb the surplus neutrons to hold the multiplication
factor at exactly **1**.
**India's three-stage programme.** PHWRs on natural uranium; **fast breeders** on the
plutonium they produce; and finally **thorium**-based reactors ✓ Kaiga belongs to the
first stage.
**A point of pride.** Kaiga Unit 1 held the world record for **continuous operation** -
962 days without a shutdown, from May 2016 to December 2018 ✓
∴ power reactor.

The cycle is a **rectangle** on the P-V diagram, so the work is simply its **area**.
**Step 1 — read the corners.**
A: (**V, P**) ✓
B: (**V, 2P**) ✓
C: (**2V, 2P**) ✓
D: (**2V, P**) ✓
**Step 2 — find the area.**
width along V = 2V − V = **V** ✓
height along P = 2P − P = **P** ✓
area = **PV** ✓
**Step 3 — fix the sign.** The path A → B → C → D → A runs **clockwise** ✓ so the work
done **by** the gas is **positive**:
W = **PV** ✓
**Why the area gives the work.** For any process W = ∫P dV ✓ Round a closed loop the
integral is the **enclosed area**, with the expansions contributing positively and the
compressions negatively.
**The process-by-process check.**
**A → B** at constant V: ΔV = 0, so **W = 0** ✓
**B → C** at constant P = 2P, expanding from V to 2V: W = **2P x V = 2PV** ✓
**C → D** at constant V: **W = 0** ✓
**D → A** at constant P, compressing from 2V to V: W = **−PV** ✓
total = 2PV − PV = **PV** ✓ confirming the area.
**Why clockwise means positive.** The expansion happens at the **higher** pressure and
the compression at the lower ✓ so more work is got out than is put back. This is a
**heat engine**; run anticlockwise it would be a refrigerator.
**The first law round the cycle.** ΔU = **0**, since the gas returns to its initial
state ✓ so
Q = W = **PV** ✓ All the net heat absorbed is converted to work over the cycle.
**Why the gas being monatomic does not affect the work.** Work depends only on the
**P-V path** ✓ The monatomic nature (C_V = 3R/2) matters for the heat exchanged in each
individual step and for the temperatures, but not for the enclosed area.
**The temperatures at the corners.** Using PV = nRT, with T_A = T:
A: **T** ✓ B: **2T** ✓ C: **4T** ✓ D: **2T** ✓
The gas is hottest at C, as expected at the top right of the diagram.
**The efficiency, for interest.** Heat enters along A → B and B → C:
Q_in = nC_VΔT + nC_PΔT = (3/2)PV + (5/2)(2PV) = **6·5PV** ✓
η = PV/6·5PV = **15·4%** ✓ far below the Carnot value of 1 − T/4T = 75%, as any
non-Carnot cycle must be.
**Reading the distractors.** **2PV** ✗ counts only the expansion and forgets the work
returned. **½PV** ✗ treats the rectangle as a triangle, and **4PV** ✗ uses the wrong
dimensions ✓
∴ PV.

Every electromagnetic wave travels in vacuum at **c** - that is what they all share.
**Step 1 — recall the defining property.** In free space
c = **1/√(µ₀ε₀)** = **3 x 10⁸ m s⁻¹** ✓
and this involves **no** reference to frequency or wavelength, so it is the same for all.
**Step 2 — see what differs.** Frequency, wavelength, energy and photon momentum all
vary across the spectrum ✓
**Step 3 — conclude.** They have the same **velocity** ✓
**The spectrum, in order of increasing frequency.**
radio **10⁴ Hz** → microwave → infrared → **visible 4-8 x 10¹⁴ Hz** → ultraviolet →
X-rays → gamma rays **10²⁰ Hz and beyond** ✓
More than sixteen decades of frequency - yet every one travels at precisely c.
**The relation that ties them.**
c = **fλ** ✓ so a high frequency means a short wavelength, the product always 3 x 10⁸.
Radio at 10⁶ Hz has λ = 300 m; gamma rays at 10²⁰ Hz have λ = 3 x 10⁻¹² m.
**The photon energy.**
E = **hf** ✓ so a gamma photon carries 10¹⁴ times the energy of a radio photon - which
is why one damages DNA and the other does not.
**Why Maxwell's result was so startling.** He computed 1/√(µ₀ε₀) from purely
**electrical and magnetic** measurements and found it equal to the measured speed of
**light** ✓ "We can scarcely avoid the inference", he wrote in 1865, "that light
consists in the transverse undulations of the same medium which is the cause of
electric and magnetic phenomena."
**Why the speed is the same for all frequencies in vacuum.** Vacuum is
**non-dispersive** ✓ µ₀ and ε₀ are constants, with no frequency dependence. In **matter**
this fails: the refractive index varies with frequency, which is **dispersion** - the
reason a prism makes a spectrum.
**The observational confirmation.** Light from a distant **supernova** arrives in all
colours **simultaneously** ✓ Even a tiny frequency dependence would smear the arrival
over years. Gamma-ray burst observations now constrain any variation to one part in
10¹⁵.
**Why c is now a defined constant.** Since 1983 the metre is **defined** by fixing
c = **299 792 458 m s⁻¹** exactly ✓ so the speed of light is no longer measured; it
defines the unit of length.
**Reading the distractors.** **Frequency** ✗, **wavelength** ✗ and **energy** ✗ are
precisely the quantities that **distinguish** one part of the spectrum from another ✓ If
they were the same, there would be only one kind of electromagnetic wave.
∴ Velocity.

Momentum conservation fixes the speeds; then compute the larger fragment's kinetic
energy.
**Step 1 — find the masses.** 20 kg split in the ratio 2 : 3:
smaller = (2/5) x 20 = **8 kg** ✓
larger = (3/5) x 20 = **12 kg** ✓
**Step 2 — apply conservation of momentum.** The shell was at **rest**, so the total
momentum stays **zero**:
m₁v₁ = m₂v₂ ✓
8 x 6 = 12 x v₂ ✓
**Step 3 — solve for the larger fragment's speed.**
v₂ = 48/12 = **4 m s⁻¹** ✓
**Step 4 — find its kinetic energy.**
K = ½m₂v₂² = ½(12)(4)² ✓
= ½(12)(16)
= **96 J** ✓
**Why the fragments fly apart in opposite directions.** The total momentum must remain
**zero** ✓ so the two momenta are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction - which
is why the heavier fragment moves **more slowly**, in inverse proportion to its mass.
**The smaller fragment's energy, for comparison.**
K₁ = ½(8)(36) = **144 J** ✓
total = 144 + 96 = **240 J** ✓ released by the explosive.
**Why the lighter fragment carries more energy.** With equal momenta,
K = **p²/2m** ✓ so the energy is **inversely** proportional to the mass. The 8 kg piece
takes 3/5 of the energy and the 12 kg piece 2/5 - in the inverse ratio of the masses,
which is a useful check: 144 : 96 = 3 : 2 ✓
**Why kinetic energy is not conserved.** The explosion **releases** chemical energy ✓
Before: zero kinetic energy. After: 240 J. This is a **superelastic** collision run
backwards - momentum conserved, energy created from internal stores.
**Why momentum is conserved even so.** No **external** horizontal force acts during the
explosion ✓ The internal forces between the fragments are equal and opposite by Newton's
third law and cancel exactly.
**The energy split in general.** For a body at rest breaking into two pieces,
K₁/K₂ = **m₂/m₁** ✓ Here 12/8 = 1·5 = 144/96 ✓
**Where this matters.** **Alpha decay**: the light alpha particle carries nearly all the
energy, the heavy recoiling nucleus very little ✓ The same arithmetic, on a nuclear
scale. It is also why a rifle's recoil is gentle while the bullet is lethal.
**Reading the distractors.** **144 J** ✗ is the **smaller** fragment's energy - the
intended trap. **360 J** ✗ and **216 J** ✗ use the wrong mass or the wrong speed ✓
∴ 96 J.
